header: TRAINS OF ONE NAME THAT GO DIFFERENT WAYS. The Poorva Express is two trains between Howrah and New Delhi: 12303 runs by PATNA (Mon, Tue, Fri, Sat) and 12381 by GAYA (Wed, Thu, Sun). On the card they showed as two lines of the same name, with only the days to tell them apart; I made each line say which way it goes ("via Patna", "via Gaya"). The same is done for every other such case found at Durgapur and Asansol (21 Nov 2026: the 387 trains of the two timetables, grouped by name, where the stop lists show different routes): Poorva Express (Howrah to Shakurbasti) 12303 via Patna, 12381 via Gaya Purvanchal Express (Kolkata to Gorakhpur) 15047 via Siwan, 15049 via Ballia, 15051 via Bettiah (three trains, three routes after Muzaffarpur/Hajipur) Khatipura special (to Khatipura) 03007 via Gaya (from Howrah), 09710 via Patna (from Kolkata) The evidence is routeVia.evidence.json: the stops of each train after Asansol, from RailRadar's timetable (the app's own fare-leg tables). Each entry names ONE station (`code`) that the train calls at and none of its `rivals` (the other trains of its name that go a different way) does; routeVia.selftest.tsx checks that against the evidence, so I list a train here only with its stops in front of me, never from memory. NOT listed, and why: the trains in the other direction (12304 and 12382, 15048, 15050 and 15052: their stops after Durgapur are only Barddhaman and Howrah or Kolkata, which do not show the route); the pair of Amrit Bharat Express 03009 and 13065 (Howrah to Anand Vihar), whose stops are the same but whose distances differ by 122 km between Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Jn and Varanasi (one of them takes a different line there, which the stops cannot name); special trains whose stops were not collected. I leave them as they were until their stops are checked. Pure.

symbols.name: viaOf
doc: Returns the route note of a train number, or null when none was checked.

behaviours: every train in the table has its stop list in the evidence
each train's via station is one it calls at, and NONE of its rivals calls there (so the name tells the trains apart)
the via word is the place's name, and no two trains of one group share it (Poorva: Patna, Gaya; Purvanchal: Siwan, Ballia, Bettiah; Khatipura: Gaya, Patna)
12303 goes by Patna and not Gaya; 12381 by Gaya and not Patna (the Poorva Express)
the three Purvanchal Expresses to Gorakhpur: 15047 calls at Siwan (not Ballia, not Bettiah), 15049 at Ballia, 15051 at Bettiah
the Khatipura specials: 03007 calls at Gaya and not Patna, 09710 at Patna and not Gaya
nothing is said for a train whose route was not checked (the return trains 12304, 12382, 15048, 15050, 15052; the Amrit Bharat pair 03009 and 13065; any other number)
each hover note names the route's own main stops and where the other trains of the name go
the fare finder's line says 'via Patna' for 12303 and 'via Gaya' for 12381, before 'runs on to', and says nothing for another train
the Durgapur card's line for Poorva Express 12303 says via Patna (a hover note too); a train with no checked route says nothing
